description:
AUDITED at clean origin/main a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83.

## Goal

A same-callee specialization that has a complete wider stand-in must not remain as a runtime destination when the dispatch seat could never safely place the narrow specialization first. Legal target-arrival permutations must not re-arm a blind-escape seat merely because a refined runtime predicate split the pair into different question groups.

Preserve every genuine specialization that the runtime can safely select first.

## Current state

`routable_alternatives` projects observable inputs, partitions targets with `question_groups`, and passes those groups to `unroutable_alternatives`. `unroutable_alternatives` searches for a stand-in only within each group.

That restriction loses fz-kdt.118's elimination whenever a refined predicate gives a contained same-callee pair different questions. The baseline unit `an_arm_whose_head_overlaps_a_wider_one_is_seated_after_it` demonstrates the minimal shape:

- narrow surface: `[int]`
- wider surface: `[int | :ok]`
- same callee and otherwise identical inputs
- overlapping list-head predicates; the tail remains erased

Both targets survive. The wider arm must be seated first because `[1, :ok]` passes the narrow head test but is outside the narrow body surface. With a third arm that neither covers nor is covered, the insertion pass stops at that arm; the legal `[narrow, blocker, wide]` arrival therefore leaves the narrow arm ahead of its stand-in.

The settled blind-escape census contains 3 entries, while the baseline source records 5 under `arms:3`; the two additions are this split-group narrow-arm population.

The original "same callee + contained test + contained surface" rule is insufficient: distinguishable precision arms such as `:timeout` beside `any` must survive and be seated narrow-first. The drop must be defined through the same safety relation as seating.

## Rule

Factor the seat relation into one shared operation:

```text
seats_before(x, y) =
    covers(x, y)
    && (!covers(y, x) || strictly_inside(test(x), test(y)))
```

Define a strict stand-in:

```text
stands_in_for(wide, narrow) =
    same_callee(wide, narrow)
    && surface(narrow) strictly contained in surface(wide)
    && test(narrow) contained in test(wide)
```

Then:

```text
unroutable(narrow) =
    exists wide != narrow:
        stands_in_for(wide, narrow)
        && !seats_before(narrow, wide)
```

This retains a narrow specialization whenever the runtime predicate and surface make narrow-first a safe precision seat. It removes the arm only when its stand-in is complete and the seat itself says the narrow arm may not pass it.

Project runtime questions and observable surfaces once in `routable_alternatives`, and pass those projections to both elimination and specificity seating. Remove the question-group parameter from `unroutable_alternatives`; question groups remain an input to seating, not the boundary of stand-in discovery.

## Safety obligations

Prove the result relative to a legal pre-drop arrival: each removed arm must receive no value when inserted after the surviving seated arms, because it cannot pass its stand-in.

Also cover group dissolution explicitly. Removing a member can change question-group composition and therefore the group-product `covers` relation. Pin a case where a removed arm shared a question with another survivor and prove that post-drop reseating cannot route an overlapping value to an incompatible or different-callee body. If that cannot be established locally, split the semantic ambiguity into its own blocking ticket rather than silently accepting the reroute.

Do not claim recovery on `enum_map_family`, `00277`, or any other fixture without a fresh baseline-to-head census showing the relevant same-callee contained pairs.

## Signal

1. Rewrite the overlapping-head unit so `[int]` is removed beside `[int | :ok]` in both arrival orders.
2. Rewrite the three-arm list-head test so the covered narrow arm is removed in all six arrivals, including `[narrow, blocker,wide]`.
3. Preserve a separating precision boundary such as `int` beside `int | float`: both survive and the narrow arm seats first.
4. Preserve the existing `:timeout` beside `any` specialization.
5. Add a degraded-predicate boundary where surface containment does not imply test containment; the narrow arm must survive.
6. Run the blind-escape census under settled order and every named arm seed, comparing named unordered pairs per setting. The split-group additions must disappear without re-blessing unrelated overlap-without-containment residue.
7. Census dispatch sites, arm lines, executables, and behavior independently; report only measured movers.

## Acceptance

- No cross-question same-callee arm remains when a strict stand-in exists and `seats_before(narrow, wide)` is false.
- No arm that `seats_before` would safely place first is dropped.
- The `[int]` / `[int | :ok]` narrow arm is absent for every arrival order.
- Legal arm permutations add no blind escape from this redundant-arm class.
- Existing overlap-without-containment cases remain owned separately and are neither hidden nor reclassified.
- Post-drop group dissolution is either proven routing-safe and pinned or represented by an explicit blocking ticket.
- Update `callsite_dispatch` and dispatch-matrix documentation to remove the within-one-question-group drop law and describe the shared seat/drop relation.
- Run focused unit tests, the per-setting blind-escape census, behavior checks through interp/JIT/AOT for every artifact mover, `cargo fmt --check`, clippy with warnings denied, `cargo test --lib`, and the fixture matrix.

title: Drop a cross-question redundant arm only when the dispatch seat cannot safely put it ahead of its stand-in
